Senses.Explanation: The whole function is the complete operative member contrasted with the whole body in body-and-function explanations and case appraisal. Juelang Daosheng and Yongming Yanshou formulate the body/function relation; Xueyan Zuqin assigns one cited line to the whole body and another to the whole function. The label appraises completeness of operation; it does not mean that every possible action is occurring.

Senses.Explanation: To use entirely is to apply one’s strength, conscious intention, or attention without holding part back. Yongjue Yuanxian applies the phrase to work on one saying; Chuiwan Guangzhen to conscious intention in learning calligraphy; Puan Yinsu to attention in an instruction. This compositional verb does not by itself name the technical whole function.
